fulfillment_judgment.auxiliary_material: Preliminary results from the first nine patients indicate the intervention is feasible and safe, with microbiome engraftment observed in 4/7 patients via 16S rRNA sequencing. However, no objective tumor responses were recorded in this early cohort, with most patients achieving stable disease or progressive disease. This data characterizes the current evidence level as early-phase exploratory rather than confirmatory.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this study to illustrate the current early-phase status of microbiome-ICI combination trials in the review. To fulfill the gap, conduct a systematic search of ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP using filters for Phase III, randomized controlled trials, solid tumours, and microbiome interventions. Document the search date, filters, and results. If no Phase III trials are found, cite this study as an example of the existing lower-phase landscape while formally recording the absence of Phase III data.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The specific success criterion requiring identification of Phase III randomized controlled trial registry numbers is not met by this material, as the identified trial is Phase IIa. Additionally, the material does not document a comprehensive search strategy across ClinicalTrials.gov or WHO ICTRP to confirm the absence of Phase III trials.
fulfillment_judgment.useful_material: This study reports a registered clinical trial (NCT05286294) evaluating a microbiome intervention (fecal microbial transplantation) combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors in solid tumour patients. The authors explicitly define the design as a single-arm phase IIa basket trial, not a Phase III randomized controlled trial. The trial includes multiple solid tumour indications such as metastatic melanoma, renal clear cell carcinoma, and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

record_identity.title: 669 MITRIC: microbiota transplant to cancer patients progressing on immunotherapy using feces from clinical responders
